english: Let $\overrightarrow{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}=\hat{i}$. Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be the real numbers such that $-7\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+34\hat{k}=x\,\overrightarrow{a}+y\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}\right)+z\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}\right)\right)$. Then the value of $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\overrightarrow{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{b}=\hat{i}$ है। माना कि $x$, $y$, $z$ वे वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं जिनके लिए $-7\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+34\hat{k}=x\,\overrightarrow{a}+y\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}\right)+z\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\left(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}\right)\right)$ है। तब $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The three vectors are mutually perpendicular, hence non-coplanar, so $x,y,z$ are unique and each is found by one dot product. Let $\overrightarrow{r}=-7\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+34\hat{k}$:
solution_full: Compute the vectors of the combination: $\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\times\hat{i}=2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ (since $\hat{j}\times\hat{i}=-\hat{k}$, $\hat{k}\times\hat{i}=\hat{j}$).

$\overrightarrow{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}$, and $\overrightarrow{a}\times(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b})$ is perpendicular to both $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}$. Being non-zero and mutually perpendicular, the three vectors are non-coplanar, so every vector in space is a unique linear combination of them.

Let $\overrightarrow{r}=-7\hat{i}+10\hat{j}+34\hat{k}$. Taking the dot product of $\overrightarrow{r}=x\overrightarrow{a}+y(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b})+z(\overrightarrow{a}\times(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b}))$ with each vector kills the other two terms.
originality_note: New: the basis is a, a x b, a x (a x b), which is orthogonal, so the coefficients of the linear combination come from single dot products instead of a 3x3 system (way 4: hidden orthogonality). Closest known: expressing a vector as x a + y b + z c for three given vectors. Different because: the basis is built from cross products and the student must see its orthogonality (or else solve a 3x3 system).

concept_use.Linear combination theorem in space: r is written uniquely as x a + y (a x b) + z (a x (a x b)) because these three vectors are non-coplanar; coefficients from the dot products.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Uniqueness of x, y, z is guaranteed (non-coplanar vectors), so 'the real numbers' is justified. Changed: No change.
key_step: Building a x b and a x (a x b) and using their mutual perpendicularity to read off the coefficients.
justification: Routine multi-step: two cross products (or a triple-product expansion), then three dot products; nothing non-standard. Like 2024-P2-Q11 (L0) in idea but with a longer chain, so L2 as 2026-P2-Q1 (L2).
